mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 3.0% (FEDFUNDS <= 3.0%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because a low interest rate environment encourages equity valuation via lower discount rates and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 3.0% (i.e., positive returns in <= 60% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5pp in 3 months) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This is because monetary tightening increases discount rates and reduces risk appetite, leading to equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5pp in the past 3 months (i.e., negative returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0% (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) and the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days are negative. This is because the co-occurrence of monetary tightening and labor market weakness signals an economic downturn, leading to equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and UNRATE > 5.0% (i.e., negative returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by UNRATE < 4.5% and GDP growth > 2% in the latest quarter), the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days are positive. This is because the economy is in a strong growth phase with low unemployment, which supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and GDPC1 growth > 2% in the last quarter
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5% and GDPC1 growth > 2% (i.e., positive returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production exceeding 2% over the past 3 months (INDPRO fall > 2% in 3 months) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This is because a sharp drop in industrial output signals an imminent economic slowdown, leading to equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO fell by more than 2% in the past 3 months (i.e., negative returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate (UNRATE falling in the last 3 months) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because a falling unemployment rate indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports economic growth and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has fallen in the last 3 months (i.e., positive returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts exceeding 3% over the past 3 months (HOUST fall > 3% in 3 months) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This is because a sharp drop in housing activity signals a weakening economy, leading to equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST fell by more than 3% in the past 3 months (i.e., negative returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the Consumer Price Index exceeding 0.3 percentage points over the past 3 months (CPIAUCSL rise > 0.3pp in 3 months) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This is because rising inflation may trigger monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rose by more than 0.3pp in the past 3 months (i.e., negative returns in <= 40% of cases), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
